description:
deviation.rs:608-625 and DeviationStore::add use str::to_lowercase (Unicode default case mapping) on both the stored substring AND the cert-side rendered DN, not make_ascii_lowercase. The case-folding-is-unicode-aware_via_to_lowercase test pins the behavior and the test commentary calls out that pre-fix make_ascii_lowercase silently mis-matched 'Müller' vs 'müller'.

Defense: real-world CA DNs in Europe and East Asia routinely contain non-ASCII characters (Bundesdruckerei, Caisse des Dépôts, Polish/Czech CAs). An ASCII-only fold would silently fail to match them — exactly the silent-no-match shape the workspace test discipline rules out.

The cost is one fresh String allocation per match call. Documented as acceptable; caller-side caching is the recommended remedy if profiling ever shows it's hot.

What a contributor might suggest changing: 'to_lowercase allocates, use make_ascii_lowercase'. Counter-argument: make_ascii_lowercase is wrong on non-ASCII input — it leaves multi-byte chars untouched, so 'MÜLLER' folds to 'mÜller', not 'müller'. The allocation cost is real but bounded; correctness comes first.

Lock this in.
title: Unicode-aware case folding in issuer_dn_contains (PKIX-hy2e.8)
